nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.confidence }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Deliver Answer + Log to Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Request Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Escalate to Human Queue
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#ai-ops) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Join Outcomes
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

# Answer user questions: Slack + AI agent

**Pattern:** Chatbot Responder · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Chat

## Overview

Answers in a chat window, and covers multi-tool-agent work end to end across Slack and Google Sheets.

It moves through 11 working steps, in this order:

1. When Chat Message Received
2. Reason & Act (AI Agent)
3. OpenAI Chat Model
4. Search Reference Wiki
5. Run Calculations
6. Conversation Memory
7. Shape Agent Output
8. Confident Enough?
9. Deliver Answer + Log to Google Sheets
10. Escalate to Human Queue
11. Join Outcomes

## Why it exists

Doing multi-tool-agent work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

When Chat Message Received → Reason & Act (AI Agent) → OpenAI Chat Model → Search Reference Wiki → Run Calculations → Conversation Memory → Shape Agent Output → Confident Enough? → Deliver Answer + Log to Google Sheets → Escalate to Human Queue → Join Outcomes

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Google Sheets aligned by hand for multi-tool agent
- Multi-tool agent work that needs a judgement call per item before it reaches Slack
- Multi-tool-agent conversations in Slack you would rather not staff around the clock
- Multi-tool agent work where "Reason & Act (AI Agent)" is still a manual step before Slack

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Google Sheets in step for multi-tool agent, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Slack or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 11 nodes in this multi-tool-agent build
- Branches rejoin before Slack, so a multi-tool-agent run reports once rather than 11 times
- The multi-tool-agent AI step is isolated from Slack, so models swap without touching the other 11 nodes
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 11 nodes for multi-tool agent before wiring Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; OpenAI API key; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Uses an AI Agent, not a fixed Chain, because the assistant must choose which tool answers the question — a Chain would need one hard-coded branch per tool. The 'Confident Enough?' gate after the agent routes low-confidence answers to a human queue instead of shipping an uncertain answer: a little latency traded for not eroding trust.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Add one more tool to the pool with a clear one-line description and watch how the agent decides to use it.
2. Change the confidence threshold on 'Confident Enough?' and see how often answers get escalated to a human.
3. Swap the Think tool for a Vector Store tool wired to a real knowledge base and turn this into RAG.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenAI API key**
platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.
_Gotcha:_ Needs billing set up; a brand-new key with no credit returns 429 immediately.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your multi-tool agent process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole multi-tool-agent payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
